Today's TL;DRRegimeMIXED
Markets are caught between a dovish macro pivot from a shockingly weak July jobs report and escalating geopolitical tensions around Iran's Strait of Hormuz. Equities hit new highs on rate-cut expectations but face headwinds from AI security failures, trade tariff escalation, and upcoming CPI data. The bond market is skeptical of Treasury Secretary Bessent's yield-cap efforts, while commodities rally on supply disruption risks. Crypto surges on institutional inflows and dovish macro but stalls at resistance. FX sees coordinated EM defense and unprecedented U.S.-Japan yen intervention. The cross-asset picture is a regime of high uncertainty with opposing forces.

×12 · 45 steps
AI data center optical connections are driving robust demand for silicon photonics and optical transceivers, with the optical connectivity market expected to grow at a 57% unit CAGR from 2025 to 2028 and total demand 8x by 2030. The datacom optical TAM is forecast to increase by $14bn from 2026 to 2028, with NPO/CPO market reaching $18bn+ by end of decade. Analog IC content per optical transceiver is estimated at $5-10, and SG Micro's optical module-related sales have grown 400% since 1Q25. AI infrastructure spending is accelerating, with Big Tech capex expected to grow ~100% YoY to $730bn in 2026 and surpass $1tn by 2028.

China domestic demand weakness vs easing expectations中国内需疲软与宽松预期
×6 · 22 steps
China's trade surplus reached a record $125bn in June ($1.5tn annual rate) while domestic demand is weak (1-2% growth proxy), with property prices down >30% and fiscal policy tight. This imbalance requires fiscal expansion and currency appreciation to achieve internal and external balance. China domestic demand is weakening across multiple sectors: official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.4 in July, new orders dropped to 48.5, output to 49.9, construction PMI fell to 47.0, profit margins remain under pressure.

Memory pricing upcycle内存涨价周期
×8 · 30 steps
Memory price increases are tempering enthusiasm in AMD's client PC segment and prompting Nvidia to de-spec products, creating headwinds for both semiconductor and console hardware makers. Memory demand continues to significantly outpace supply. DRAM spot prices have reached multi-decade highs, with 16Gb DDR5 at ~US$51, and NAND spot prices rallied 5-6% on 512Gb-1Tb, driven by supply reallocation to HBM and server DRAM and rush orders from OEMs. Analysts expect continued price increases, though some temper expectations.

AI-related demand, particularly for AI accelerators and HBM, is driving significant investment in ASIC design and advanced packaging, which in turn boosts demand for semiconductor equipment. Nomura reports MediaTek's ASIC sales surging to USD12-16bn in 2027E, with advanced packaging partnerships key. Goldman Sachs reports that generative AI demand continues to drive DISCO's shipments, with brisk investment in HBM4 and advanced packaging like CPO and hybrid bonding driving equipment demand. AI and datacenter demand remains robust, driving growth in semiconductor equipment and components, and spilling over into adjacent industries such as factory automation and semi capital equipment.

Pricing power and cost pass-through定价能力与成本转嫁
×6 · 23 steps
Companies differ in ability to pass on cost increases: Renesas implemented price hikes from July 1 and L'Oréal achieved volume and value growth, while Murata has only partially considered pricing adjustments due to cost increases in energy, precious metals, and labor. Companies across sectors are demonstrating pricing power by passing through higher costs, seen in Monster Beverage (planned US pricing increase), LG Uplus (higher AIDC pricing), GlobalFoundries (pricing actions), and Klaviyo (carrier-fee pass-through). Supply-demand tightness in AI hardware is enabling price increases and margin expansion: ON Semi raised prices and improved utilization from 77% to 83%, Wistron renegotiated terms and expects margin improvement.

K-Shaped AI divergenceAI与传统的K型分化
×4 · 19 steps
Global composite PMI rose +0.6pt to 52.6 in July, driven by a services rise (+0.8pt to 52.5) while manufacturing ticked down. Services input prices rose (+0.4pt to 59.9) but manufacturing input prices fell sharply (-2.3pt to 60.7), signaling diverging cost dynamics. New export orders surged in India (+2.2pt to 54.3) but collapsed in Mexico (-4.4pt to 47.5). This reinforces the K-shaped divergence between AI/Tech and traditional sectors, with high-tech manufacturing PMI staying strong while overall manufacturing contracts.

AI sector correction deleverageAI板块修正与定位去杠杆
×3 · 12 steps
The AI sector correction in July 2026 was driven by an intense positioning unwind after a momentum rally, with hedge funds and retail leverage moderating. Gross leverage reversed half its yearly increase, marking the second-largest 2-day long selling in a decade. AxJ Tech later recovered almost half its July losses. Korea leveraged ETF AUM fell from peak $53bn to $24bn; margin loans declined only 14% from peak while deposits fell 22%, pushing margin-loan-to-deposit ratio from 17% to 26%.

Chinese tax authorities are tightening tax collection across the board, including potential reductions in tax rebates for high-tech internet companies, a new 20% personal income tax on offshore insurance policy returns, a new offshore trust tax regime, and now reports that certain Chinese cities may levy a 20% tax on offshore insurance policies, suggesting a tightening that could dampen capital inflows to Hong Kong, posing headwinds to residential demand from non-local buyers. BernsteinDissent4 steps
  1. 1
    Premise卫星直连室内覆盖不行
    80 %
    It is already well established that satellite-based D2D coverage does not work inside, where 80%+ of mobile demand is located, and 65MHz of EchoStar spectrum is necessary but not sufficient to become a true nationwide mobile network and will probably need to be deployed using some form of terrestrial radio architecture (likely on towers).
    8fdf19c0d590·《US Communications Infrastructure: Everybody relax - towers aren't going anywhere, even if Elon gets creative》·2026-08-06
  2. 2
    Mechanism毫微微蜂窝范围和容量有限
    60 feet；6 users；1 km；5 km；40 km
    Femtocells have been around since the early 2000s and were wildly unsuccessful for carriers — coverage radius about 60 feet, each cell supports only ~6 users; a metrocell or picocell comparison would extend the radius to maybe 1km, versus an average tower coverage radius of ~5km today and up to 40km for a coverage build.
    8fdf19c0d590·《US Communications Infrastructure: Everybody relax - towers aren't going anywhere, even if Elon gets creative》·2026-08-06
  3. 3
    MechanismSpaceX建网规模远超宏基站
    5 x；40 x
    In a BEST case SpaceX would need 5x more small cells than towers for nationwide coverage, and perhaps up to 40x; while hardware is cheaper and bandwidth/rent costs are lower, installation and deployment are far less efficient, with complex RF engineering, likely FCC issues for a new tech, multiplied local permitting, incumbent pushback, dense-urban problems and line-of-sight limitations.
    8fdf19c0d590·《US Communications Infrastructure: Everybody relax - towers aren't going anywhere, even if Elon gets creative》·2026-08-06
  4. 4
    Conclusion现有基站已有长期资产护城河
    Even if SpaceX's approach proves more capital-efficient than the legacy process, the incumbents are not starting from zero — AMT, CCI and SBAC already own long-lived macro assets and rights-of-way, wi
    Even if SpaceX's approach proves more capital-efficient than the legacy process, the incumbents are not starting from zero — AMT, CCI and SBAC already own long-lived macro assets and rights-of-way, with incremental economics driven by adding tenants and upgrading radios, while SpaceX must fund a new distributed network, acquire mobile customers at scale, build a brand in wireless, and overcome churn frictions and procurement lock-in of the Big 3 carriers.
    8fdf19c0d590·《US Communications Infrastructure: Everybody relax - towers aren't going anywhere, even if Elon gets creative》·2026-08-06

China's Disinflation and Structural Shift
China's PPI cooled for the first time since the Iran war began, and CPI also decelerated, indicating that oil shock inflationary pressures are fading. Meanwhile, China overtook the U.S. in global R&D spending, reaching $615 billion, signaling a structural competitive shift. Typhoon Dolphin caused massive disruptions in eastern China, cancelling over 1,680 flights and evacuating hundreds of thousands. These mixed signals show a disinflationary trend with long-term competitive gains but near-term weather-related economic damage.

Trade Tariff Escalation and Congressional Authorization
The U.S. Senate passed the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 by an 86-11 vote, granting President Trump unchecked authority to impose tariffs up to 100% on top trading partners, including India and China. New tariffs of up to 12.5% were imposed on Switzerland over forced-labor concerns, while the administration is processing ~$128B in tariff refunds after court losses. These moves signal a major escalation in trade war risk, affecting global supply chains and EM exports.
